answers.explanation: Each lower layer wraps everything the layer above gave it, so the outermost header belongs to the lowest layer.
That's encapsulation. The data link layer adds a trailer as well.
De-encapsulation is encapsulation in reverse: each layer strips its own header and passes the rest up.
The Frame Check Sequence is a CRC-32 of the whole frame.
Ethernet detects errors but doesn't correct them. Any recovery happens higher up, for example TCP resending a missing segment.
A switch can start forwarding as soon as it has read 6 bytes.
Most significant byte first. That's what the ! in struct.pack("!HH", …) asks for.
H is a 2-byte unsigned number, and there are two of them.
Destination MAC (6) + source MAC (6) + length (2) + FCS (4) = 18. A real Ethernet frame has the same 18 bytes of overhead, with a type field in place of the length.
Each layer only reads the header its partner layer wrote.
